catalogue-of-british-columbia-birds: Francis Kermode, curator of the provincial museum in Victoria, compiled this working list of every bird known in British Columbia around the turn of the century. Each entry names the species and notes where in the province it had been recorded. Though dry by design, the catalogue is a valuable snapshot of the region's birdlife before a century of change, prized by ornithologists and natural historians.
letters-of-anton-chekhov-to-his-family-a: The great Russian writer of plays and short stories shows his private self in these letters home. Chekhov writes of his doctor's work, his failing health, his plays like The Cherry Orchard, and small daily things — all with the same kind eye found in his tales. A close and moving self-portrait.
five-little-peppers-and-their-friends: Margaret Sidney returns to the beloved Pepper family in this warm addition to the classic children's series. Polly, Joel, Davie, Phronsie, and Ben are joined by old friends for new scrapes, kindnesses, and small adventures. Generations of young readers grew up with the Peppers, whose cheerful courage in hard times made them American favorites.
on-the-study-of-words: Richard Chenevix Trench's famous lectures reveal the hidden history inside ordinary English words. Each word, he shows, carries the story of the people who used it — their work, wars, faith, and follies. Delivered in the 1850s, these talks charmed Victorian audiences and practically invented the popular study of word origins.
stray-birds: Tagore's Stray Birds collects hundreds of tiny poems — some just a line or two — like birds alighting for a moment. On love, death, nature, and the divine, each fragment gleams with compressed wisdom. The Nobel laureate's most intimate book, it rewards readers who like to pause, ponder, and return again.
the-school-for-husbands: Molière's comedy contrasts two brothers raising two wards: one strict, one indulgent — and shows which philosophy wins in love. L'École des maris argues, amid much laughter, that trust works better than tyranny. An early Molière triumph, still fresh in its understanding of the human heart.
ruth-fielding-at-snow-camp-or-lost-in-th: Alice Emerson's plucky heroine Ruth Fielding spends a winter at Snow Camp, where snowy adventures and a backwoods mystery await. Ruth's courage and kindness carry her through in the best series tradition. A cheerful girls' adventure from the golden age of series fiction.
the-camp-fire-girls-go-motoring-or-along: Hildegard Frey's Camp Fire Girls take to the open road in this motoring adventure. Camping, mishaps, and good cheer fill a story that celebrated both the automobile and girls' new freedom. A breezy period piece from the days when motoring itself was an adventure.
history-of-the-philippine-islands: Antonio de Morga's 1609 history — written by a Spanish colonial judge who lived in Manila — is the great early account of the Philippines. His descriptions of the islands, their peoples, and the galleon trade remain a foundational source for historians. History from the age of sails and swords.
the-eustace-diamonds: Anthony Trollope's Eustace Diamonds follows Lizzie Eustace — liar, flirt, and keeper of the disputed diamonds — through society's traps. The Palliser novel's most brilliant rogue. Trollope's wickedest delight. Her lies glitter brighter than the diamonds she will not surrender. Trollope never drew a more deliciously wicked heroine.
lost-on-the-moon-or-in-quest-of-the-fiel: Roy Rockwood's boys are lost on the moon — in quest of the fabled field of diamonds — in this early science-fiction adventure. Lunar wonders, strange perils, and boyish pluck thrill young readers. Space travel from before rockets were ever dreamed of.
